quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: Section 4 is structured in our favour and meets the fallback in full (and most of the preferred). § 4(a) vests the "Works" (all drawings, documents, designs, inventions, programs, systems, data and documentation prepared by Contractor as Statement of Work product) in Clear Capital as "the property of Company," and § 11(c) (p0044) adds an express assignment of all right, title and interest in Works in progress on termination once final payment is made. § 4(b)(i)-(ii) confines Contractor's retained ownership to its own pre-existing proprietary tools, methodologies, know-how and records — permitted generic-tools/know-how retention, not a deliverables grab. § 4(c) grants us a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable licence to use, copy, modify and create derivative versions of any embedded Contractor's Information for our business operations, and § 4(d) confirms we may modify the software and engage third parties to do so without further payment. On Customer Data, there is no Vendor licence at all: our documents, software, reports, data and records are Confidential Information which "Contractor shall not use or disclose to any person, firm or entity ... without Company's express, prior written permission" (p0040), and § 5(b) expressly carves out "rights respecting programs, data and materials provided by Company" from what Contractor conveys — so the requirement that any Vendor licence in our data be limited to providing the Services is not engaged, and nothing assigns our IP or data to Contractor. No joint ownership is created; each category is "sole and exclusive" to one party. Two shortfalls against the preferred wording only, noted rather than redlined: the § 4(c) embedded-IP licence is perpetual but not expressly "irrevocable," and there is no standalone sentence confirming we retain all rights in our data (the confidentiality and § 5(b) carve-out achieve the same result in substance). Ownership under § 4(a) is conditioned on the relevant invoice having been paid, which matches the playbook's own "we own what we pay for" premise. This clause therefore sits at or above the fallback and is acceptable as drafted.

quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.

The licence is helpfully perpetual, royalty-free and sublicensable, but it fails both fallback elements (affiliates on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor) on material terms. verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete in operative language: affiliate coverage on written notice and M&A successor transferability are both inside the Section 4(c) grant, not merely promised in the margin comment. Preferred level fails on three elements: no contractor coverage, no "irrevocable", and successor transferability narrowed to M&A only. To reach preferred the drafter would add "and its contractors acting on its behalf", insert "irrevocable" among the licence adjectives, and broaden "a successor in a merger or acquisition" to Customer's successors generally. Minimality holds: only the two fallback features were added to an existing grant; the favourable retained terms (royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable, business-operations scope) are untouched, nothing outside the checklist (no survival tail, expense or procedure language) is added, and no word was deleted. The "without Contractor's approval" tag is the permitted direct form rather than a broad notwithstanding override of Section 10, so it does not breach the minimality boundary on assignment overrides. Intent preserved: Section 10 is left intact and is not contradicted — it governs assignment of the Agreement and its obligations, whereas the new words permit transfer of a specific licence right; no new assignment exception is granted to Contractor, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created ("affiliates" is used in its ordinary sense, consistent with the Agreement's undefined usage). Minor drafting nit for the record, not a failure: "a successor" is unqualified as to which party's successor; "a successor to Company" would remove any ambiguity.

The only competition-adjacent language in § 4(b) runs the other way: Company acknowledges Contractor's freedom to serve other clients, which is a restriction-free acknowledgment binding us only to tolerate Contractor's other business. § 4(b)(ii) limits our resale or other use of Contractor's own pre-existing proprietary materials to the software we receive, but that is ordinary licence-scope wording for Vendor IP, not a field-of-use or non-compete restriction on our own products or business, and § 4(c) separately licenses Contractor's Information for our business operations. § 13 is a mutual personnel non-solicitation, which is a distinct commercial term and is not flagged here as a non-compete. quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
rationale: The Agreement runs indefinitely (§ 2: "shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6"), and the only convenience right, in § 6(a), is available solely "at any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding". Once an engagement is under way — precisely when an exit matters — Company has no right to terminate for convenience, and § 6(b) is confined to uncured material breach. That absence of any Customer convenience right in an open-ended term fails both the preferred and fallback positions, and the fallback's "end of a term" anchor has no application in an indefinite MSA. We therefore added, at the preferred level, an express right in operative language for Company to terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience on thirty (30) days' advance written notice, with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, plus an express bar on Contractor convenience termination while any Statement of Work is outstanding (mutually exclusive with retained § 6(a), so Contractor's 15-day right survives only when nothing is in progress). Sections 2, 6(a) and 6(b) are preserved verbatim, including the Customer-favourable mutual 15-day gap-period right.

quote: 10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: Section 10 is the only assignment provision; there is no change-of-control language anywhere and no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on our change of control (Section 6 contains only mutual convenience and breach terminations), so the walk-away trigger is not present. However, the clause subjects every assignment, including an assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, to the other party's prior consent. It therefore fails the fallback position, which requires a mutual successor-assignment right exercisable on written notice, even though it already satisfies the fallback's consent and reasonableness elements for other assignments. We propose the shortest fix at the fallback level: a mutual successor carve-out on written notice, leaving the consent standard intact for all other assignments (no affiliate exception is added, consistent with the fallback).

verification.notes: Position-complete at the fallback level: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (mutual successor right, written notice, retained consent gate, retained reasonableness standard). The deviation call is correct because the unamended clause subjected successor assignments to the counterparty's consent, failing the fallback's mutual successor right. Preferred level is not reached: no affiliate carve-out for Customer, no bar on Vendor assigning to a Customer competitor, and the mutual successor carve-out now allows Vendor to assign to its own successor without Customer consent. If the preferred position is later pursued, make the carve-out one-way (Company only), add "or to an affiliate", and add "and in no event to a competitor of Company". Walk-away is not engaged: there is no change-of-control provision and no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on Customer's change of control, so the sixth preferred element is satisfied by absence and required no edit. Minimal: a single appended sentence, nothing deleted, no survival tail, expense language, or extra procedure. The "Notwithstanding the foregoing" opener is scoped to the immediately preceding sentence rather than functioning as a broad agreement-wide override, so it does not trip the non-minimal override boundary, though a direct "without the other party's consent" formulation would be equally tight. Preserves intent: the retained consent standard, the subcontracting restriction, and Section 6's termination mechanics all survive without contradiction; the new sentence leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference.

quote: Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work.

Because no audit right binds Customer, the frequency, notice, cost-allocation and no-system-access limits have nothing to attach to and the rule is satisfied by absence; we do not volunteer an audit right in order to qualify it, since that would weaken us. Targeted searches for "most favoured/favored", "favorable", "right to match", "other customers/clients" and "exclusive" returned no obligation requiring Clear Capital to extend to RadialSpark any terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers, and §§ 1, 4, 5, 6 and 7 contain no such covenant. The single preferred element — no MFN obligation on Customer benefiting Vendor — is therefore satisfied at the preferred level, so no redline is proposed. Noted only in passing (not a deviation under this rule): § 3(b) lets Contractor change rates on 30 days' notice, which is a pricing-stability point for the pricing rule rather than an MFN issue.

quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.

Services are engaged "on a task by task basis" under individually agreed Statements of Work (p0004), compensation is on a time-and-materials basis as set out in each Statement of Work (p0013), and on termination Contractor is paid only fees and expenses "incurred or earned ... through the effective date of such termination" (p0033). quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

Section 5(c)'s non-infringement warranty does not fund the defence or damages of a third-party IP claim. Absence of any Vendor IP indemnity is walk-away territory, so we inserted our fallback position as new Section 7(d): a Contractor third-party IP indemnity with the customary Company-modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace remedies with a refund of fees paid if none is commercially available, and a super-cap of three times annual fees expressed to override the Section 7(a) fees-paid cap so the indemnity is not swallowed by it. Preferred level is not reached: no duty to defend, no affiliates as indemnified parties, no breach-of-law / data-breach / gross-negligence-or-wilful-misconduct limbs, and no notice, defence-control or cooperation procedure. The Customer-indemnity element is met only vacuously because the Agreement imposes no indemnity on Company. Minimality holds: the redline is a single concise insertion after the existing 7(c), deletes nothing, and adds no survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate outside the fallback checklist. The narrow "Notwithstanding Paragraph 7(a)" carve-out is necessary rather than surplus, because without it the 7(a) fees-paid cap would swallow the required 3x super-cap; it is targeted at the specific cap rather than a broad override. Intent is preserved: the 7(a) and 7(b) allocations, the Paragraph 9 carve-out and the 7(c) attorneys'-fees waiver survive without contradiction; the Section 5(c) non-infringement warranty is complementary, and the terms used (Services, Works, Company, Contractor) are already defined in the Agreement, leaving no dangling reference. To reach preferred the drafter would need to state "USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate", raise E&O to USD 2,000,000 and cyber to USD 5,000,000. Minimality holds: the edit is a single conjunctive insertion into the existing sentence; workers' compensation, CGL, E&O, the "in connection with the provision of Services" scope, the certificates mechanic and the material-change notice are all retained verbatim, and no survival tail, at-own-expense language or other model-language extras were imported. Intent is preserved: the new cover sits inside the existing term-long obligation and is captured by "evidencing the above coverage", leaving no undefined term, dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence. Classification as a deviation is supportable because the clause as drafted failed the fallback outright (no cyber cover at all) for a contractor that accesses Company confidential records and computer systems.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap mutual at 12 months' fees and carve out indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

quote: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Section 7(a) caps both parties, but the basis is not 12 months' fees: Contractor's cap is only the fees paid for the particular Services under the relevant Statement of Work, which on a long or multi-SOW engagement can fall well below twelve months' fees. The only carve-out points to "PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF", which is the Independent Contractor clause, so it is a dangling reference and the Agreement contains no indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct carve-out (Section 8 confidentiality obligations sit inside the cap). That fails the fallback on material terms. We therefore target the fallback: a mutual cap of fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, with Excluded Claims (indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence, wilful misconduct) outside the cap. The mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages in 7(b) is untouched.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: the cap is mutual, based on fees paid in the twelve months preceding the claim, and indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are lifted out via a defined Excluded Claims term. Preferred level is not reached: (i) no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor and the basis is 'fees paid' rather than 'fees paid or payable'; (ii) no data protection/security carve-out; (iii) no fraud carve-out; (iv) no carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP; (v) no statement that Company's payment obligations are not 'damages' subject to the cap. To reach preferred, add the floor and 'paid or payable', and extend Excluded Claims to data protection/security breach, fraud and IP infringement, plus a sentence that Company's obligation to pay fees due is not subject to the cap. Claimed finding status 'deviation' is correct on the original: the Contractor-side cap was limited to fees paid under the particular Statement of Work (potentially far below twelve months' fees) and the sole exception pointed to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor), leaving indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct inside the cap. Minimality holds: the edit rewrites only the cap sentence and its carve-out mechanic — both squarely within the selected elements — retains the Statement of Work reference and leaves 7(b)'s mutual consequential-damages exclusion untouched; no extras (survival tails, procedures, extra damages categories) were added. Caveat for the drafter: if Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor) contains a Contractor tax or status indemnity, confirm it is captured by 'INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS' so the deleted exception does not narrow existing Customer-favourable protection. Intent preserved: the definition of Fees/Services and SOW mechanics are unaffected, the broken/mismatched 'PARAGRAPH 9' cross-reference is cured by a self-contained Excluded Claims definition, and no dangling term or contradictory retained sentence is left.
